K_problems.problem: Screen 1 has 25 required fields with no way to save part-way, plus a 10-minute inactivity timeout
K_problems.why: With NVDA, tabbing through 25 fields, reading each label and checking jargon like ISIC takes me 20 to 30 minutes. I'll stop to look up a trade licence number or an email address and lose everything. Timeouts with no warning and no way to extend them fail WCAG 2.2.1. This alone would make me quit.

K_problems.problem: Required fields are marked only with '*'
K_problems.why: Unless there is aria-required, NVDA reads 'star' or nothing. With 25 asterisks, that marker means nothing to me anyway.

K_problems.problem: Jargon labels: 'EngagementSpec', 'EvidenceItems', 'M02 critical gaps', 'provenance class: observed', 'sales_tx', 'mkt_spend_ts'
K_problems.why: NVDA reads these as gibberish like 'sales underscore t x'. I can't skim them visually, so every unclear label costs me several re-reads. They're also not about my problem: I'm in logistics, and it asks for sales and marketing data.

K_problems.problem: Gap status shown only by red and green dots
K_problems.why: I can't see colour at all. NVDA reads 'bullet' or 'black circle', so I have no idea which gaps are missing and which are done. This fails WCAG 1.4.1.

K_problems.problem: Upload works only by drag-and-drop ('Drag files here') with no button
K_problems.why: This is a hard blocker. I can't drag anything with a keyboard, and there's no file input to focus. I can't upload my data at all.

K_problems.problem: Errors appear as a 3-second toast saying 'Error 422: schema mismatch'
K_problems.why: If it isn't in an aria-live region, NVDA never says it. If it is, it may be cut off by other speech and then it's gone. The text doesn't say which column is wrong or how to fix it, and I can't find it again later.

K_problems.problem: Mission, Vision, Risk appetite (1–10), Preferred methodology
K_problems.why: These are consultant questions, not mine. A 1–10 slider is often not keyboard accessible, and I can't answer it meaningfully anyway.

K_problems.problem: The session-timeout notice sits in the footer
K_problems.why: I reach it last, if I reach it at all, usually after I've already lost my work.

K_problems.problem: The status screen is a spinner with 'processing' and nothing else
K_problems.why: A spinner either says nothing to NVDA or says 'busy' forever. There's no estimate, no next step, no email promise and no heading structure. I can't tell if it has frozen.

K_problems.problem: No headings, landmarks or error summary are mentioned anywhere
K_problems.why: I navigate with H and D. Without structure, every screen is one flat stream of text.

K_problems.problem: Validation on one Submit with 25 fields
K_problems.why: If errors are shown only in red next to fields, with no summary and no focus moved to the first error, I'll hunt through 25 fields to find what failed.

walkthrough: Wizard step 1, company profile, 6 fields: 3–4 minutes. Fine if labelled. I need the progress bar exposed as text ('Step 1 of 5') and not only as a visual bar.
Step 2, pick a category: Operations is the obvious choice. Fine if it's radio buttons, a nightmare if it's clickable cards built from divs. Then I describe delays: 3 minutes.

Step 3, goals and KPIs, 'choose from suggestions or type': 5–8 minutes. Suggestion chips and comboboxes are often unlabelled or not announced. I get stuck figuring out whether my typed KPI was accepted.
Step 4, constraints and budget: 3 minutes. Step 5, review and submit: 3 minutes if the review is plain text with headings. Saving as a draft is a real relief.

Data page: a table of datasets with name, description, status and upload button. A proper data table is fine with table navigation (Ctrl+Alt+arrows). The risk is status shown only by colour or an icon with no text, and upload buttons all called 'Upload' with no dataset name. Downloading templates is good. Upload itself: 10–15 minutes, depending on whether the native file dialog is used.

Dashboard: this is where I struggle. Tiles of percentages read as '62%', '40%' with no context. Charts are images or canvas with no text alternative, and 'messages' is buried. I don't know what to do next or whether I'm waiting. 10+ minutes of wandering, and I'd likely email someone to ask.

Report: a formal PDF/Word report. If the PDF is tagged with headings, reading order and table headers, it's great: I can jump by heading to findings. If it's an untagged export, it's unreadable, and the charts in it have no description. The online view helps if it's real HTML.
Total: roughly 50–70 minutes over two or three sessions. I'd probably finish with help at the dashboard stage.
blockers: BLOCKER if the KPI suggestion chips or category cards can't be reached or announced by keyboard
BLOCKER if dashboard charts and tiles have no text equivalent and the only 'next step' cue is visual
BLOCKER if the PDF report is untagged
Fixable: status in the data table needs text, not colour only
Fixable: give each upload button a dataset-specific accessible name
Fixable: announce the progress bar as 'Step X of 5'
Fixable: add a confidence appendix summary at each finding instead of only in the back
C.quote: The wizard I can manage, forms are my bread and butter. But then the dashboard reads me a list of percentages and I'm sitting there asking, 62 percent of what, and is it my turn?

walkthrough: I land on the page and press H. The 'Your next step' card is first, so I hear the one thing I need to do: about 30 seconds. This is exactly how I want to start.

Describe the problem in one text box: 'On-time delivery dropped from 94% to 86% since July, we suspect carrier X and the new depot': 4 minutes. 3–5 follow-up questions appear on the same page. I need them announced or focus moved to them, otherwise I won't know they appeared: 5 minutes.
Progress tracker: 'text + icon + step number' means NVDA can read it, as long as it's a list with the current step marked (aria-current). 1 minute.
'What we understood': I read it by heading and fix one line with its Edit link: 3 minutes. Every Edit link needs a unique name, like 'Edit suspected cause', not ten links all called 'Edit'.

Data checklist: plain-word names, why it's needed, how to get it, Must have or Helpful as text. With a real Upload button I upload the shipment export: 10–15 minutes. When a file fails, I need the explanation to appear inline, focus to move to it, and it to stay there. The 'example of a correct file' must be a table or text, not a screenshot. 'Someone else has this → invite them' is great, because our TMS admin owns the carrier scan data.
Autosave means a long session isn't scary. I leave and come back days later, and the next-step card tells me where I am.
Waiting: an email only when I need to act, with no notifications I have to catch in time.

Report: one-paragraph answer first, then steps, then 'How sure are we?' per finding in words ('Strong', with a reason). That's perfect for me because it isn't a colour badge. [Ask a question about this] per finding. Word download is the most accessible format for me. 15 minutes to read and act.
Risk: it's a long page, so I depend on a clean heading hierarchy and landmarks. Without them, it's a scrolling wall.
Total: roughly 45–60 minutes across sessions, and I'd do it myself.
blockers: No inherent blockers in the concept
Fixable, critical: a proper heading hierarchy and landmarks on the long page
Fixable: move focus to or announce dynamically inserted follow-up questions and upload errors (persistent, not a toast)
Fixable: give Edit and Upload links unique accessible names
Fixable: the progress tracker icons need text and aria-current
Fixable: example files as text or tables, not images
Fixable: any charts in the report need a data table or text summary
B.quote: Press H, hear 'Your next step: upload 2 files, about 15 minutes'. Finally someone told me what to do without me having to go hunting for it.

walkthrough: I type the problem into the chat box: 2 minutes. Then I wait for the reply. Will NVDA announce it? If the log isn't a polite live region, I hear nothing. If it is, a long reply may interrupt whatever I'm typing.

Follow-up questions, one at a time: 10 minutes of tabbing back and forth between the input and the history to re-read the last question. In browse mode, I lose my place every time new messages arrive.
Summary card with [That's right] [Change something]: fine if the buttons are labelled. But which card's 'That's right' is it, once there are three of them in the thread?

Data requests one per message, each with Upload, Connect and 'I don't have this'. After 6 requests, the thread has six identical button groups. To find the one I haven't answered, I listen through the whole thread. Stuck for 10+ minutes. Nothing tells me what's still outstanding.
Coming back after 3 days: I have to re-read the whole thread linearly to find out where I am. This is where I might abandon.

Report as a long chat message with expandable sections: expanders inside a chat log often aren't buttons with aria-expanded, and the headings in a message may be flattened. Download PDF, which may or may not be tagged. Follow-up questions in chat are nice.
Total: 60–90 minutes, much of it re-reading. A high chance I'd finish only by emailing someone 'what do you still need from me?'
blockers: BLOCKER if new messages aren't announced through a polite live region and focus is stolen or not managed
BLOCKER in practice: no outstanding-items list, so with repeated identical buttons in the thread I can't find what's pending
Fixable: give message headings and landmarks; turn each message into an article with a heading
Fixable: unique button names ('Upload last 12 months of orders')
Fixable: a 'jump to latest' or 'jump to pending' shortcut
Fixable: expandable sections as real disclosure buttons
Fixable: tagged PDF or a Word option
A.quote: Chatting is fine for a minute. But on day three, when I'm arrowing through forty messages to find which Upload button I haven't pressed yet, I'm done.

interrogation.a: Losing my work: a timeout or a form that can't be saved, after I've spent 20 minutes tabbing through it. Or an upload I can only do by dragging. Either one, and I close the tab and tell my manager the tool doesn't work for us.
interrogation.b: Each finding in words, not colour: what the delay driver is (for example 'carrier X, Zone 4, Fridays'), how sure you are and why, which of my files and how many rows it came from, the date range, and what you didn't check. Numbers I can read in a real table, not a chart image. A tagged Word or HTML version I can navigate by heading. And a clear 'do this first' with an expected effect, so I can take it to ops on Monday.
interrogation.c: In B: make the next-step card a landmark I can jump to with one key, and announce changes on it. Move focus to and keep upload errors inline, with a text example of the right columns. Give every Edit, Upload and 'Ask a question' control a unique name. Add a 'skip to report' link and a short-key list. Make Word or accessible HTML the default format, with a text summary for every chart. And let me check my upload before submitting it: 'We read 12,430 rows, columns: date, carrier, depot…'.
interrogation.d: Two ideas. First, an accessibility preference at the start ('I use a screen reader'), which switches charts to tables, removes animations, keeps messages until dismissed, and sends the report as tagged Word with alt text. Second, an audio or plain-text 'briefing' version of the report (a 2-minute read-aloud summary) plus an email digest of the next step, so I can work entirely from my inbox if the web app has problems. Also, a way for the tool to read my uploaded file back to me in a sentence before analysis, so I know it understood my columns.
